clue.text: Salt perhaps at home breaking into shanty

indicators.note: one piece breaking into another forces its way inside it

parts.note: a shanty is a sailors' work song, a sea song
at home means in

explanation.surface: A recipe-like note about salt getting into a sailors' song.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' warns that salt is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is one example of a flavouring added to food.

clue.text: Cover used in small facility's main view

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: one thing used in another is placed inside it

parts.note: facility means ease, as in doing something with ease
a cap is a covering or lid

explanation.surface: A lid fitted in a small installation, overlooking the main sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old poetic word for the sea, so the main view is a view of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or view of the sea, the main, is a marine vista.

clue.text: Man in central parts of Spain missing Cornish pasty

indicators.note: the man is put in among the other letters
the central parts are the middle letters of each of the three following words

parts.note: he stands for any man

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is going without his favourite Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of Spain, missing and Cornish are A, S and N. 'Cornish pasty' looks like a phrase, but pasty is an adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty here is the adjective for an unhealthily pale complexion.

clue.text: Book burning — smoke holds up perpetrator we're after

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower part holds up the part above it, so this piece comes last

parts.note: the culprit we are hunting is our man
a fire that is still burning is said to be in
a Havana is a Cuban cigar, something to smoke

explanation.surface: A book-burning scene in which smoke hides the arsonist the police are chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Graham Greene's 1958 spy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a Graham Greene novel, so a specific literary work.

clue.text: Breath so taken when pub hosts lottery?

indicators.note: a host holds the guest inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when the local pub runs a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath sucked inward, a gasp, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Low-down American's heart just like all the rest

parts.note: gen is slang for information, the low-down

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the inner four of American

explanation.surface: The inside story on an American's heart is that it's no different from anyone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not distinctive, shared by a whole class, is unbranded and ordinary.

clue.text: Impale vampires coming from the east?

indicators.note: in an across answer east is the right, so coming from there means read right to left

parts.note: vampire bats are bats

explanation.surface: How to deal with vampires arriving from Transylvania in the east: a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a pointed weapon or stake.

clue.text: Bottom drawer opening for trouserless philosopher

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the Swiss-French philosopher

explanation.surface: A trouserless philosopher reaches for his bottom drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is the British term for a bride's collection of linen and clothes put by for marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's stock of clothes and linen gathered before marriage is the same thing as a hope chest.

clue.text: Next to best idea volunteers ignored

indicators.note: letters ignored are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Coming close to the best idea, though the volunteers' input was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes the T and the final A of 'best idea'. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alongside something means being adjacent to it.

clue.text: Surprisingly small and useful Red Book that invited censure

indicators.note: the letters arrive in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A little red handbook turns out to be surprisingly practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges SMALL, USEFUL and RED. Baudelaire's 1857 poems were prosecuted for offending public morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Baudelaire's poetry collection was tried for obscenity, a work that drew official condemnation.

clue.text: Men after charge can't stand

indicators.note: the men come after the charge

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers, after being charged with assault, are unable to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is an assault charge in British law.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to be unable to bear it.

clue.text: Organ used in transplant that's unsafe

indicators.note: letters transplanted are moved to new positions

explanation.surface: A used organ in a transplant operation is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous is not safe.

clue.text: Work associating responsibility with farewell?

parts.note: to carry the can is to take responsibility
ta-ta is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: A job that linked taking charge with saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry the can' is a British idiom for taking the blame or responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition is a musical work, as in an opus.

clue.text: Rubbish dump's first to be rejected

parts.note: refuse is household rubbish

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The rubbish dump's first proposal was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned down has been declined.

clue.text: Author comes in — he's altered retirement plan

parts.note: to author a book is to pen it

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer arrives and announces he has changed his pension arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' is a verb here, meaning write. 'altered' rearranges COMES IN HE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension scheme is an arrangement providing income after leaving work.

clue.text: Architect hostile about very English country home

parts.note: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street

indicators.note: very and English sit about the hostile word, one each side

parts.note: ill as in ill will means hostile

explanation.surface: A hostile architect objects to a very English country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country home' looks like a rural mansion; it means the home of country music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee city is the capital of the country and western music industry.

clue.text: Nice cop?

parts.note: Nice is the French Riviera city, so a cop there is a French policeman

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, Nice looks like the adjective but is the city in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A French police officer, part of the national military police force.

clue.text: Characters in NHS, red-faced, upset about EU enjoying misfortune

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the other piece, around it
upset letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Health service staff, embarrassed and angry about Europe, take pleasure in others' failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NHS and RED-FACED to SCHADENFRDE, which goes 'about' EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The German loanword names pleasure taken in another person's bad luck.

clue.text: Movement in barrier surrounding platform

indicators.note: the barrier surrounds the platform, holding it inside

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Something shifting inside a barrier around a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement in the arts.

clue.text: An uplifting fragrance now in production

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A cheering new perfume has just gone into production.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being is emerging, beginning to be made.

clue.text: Socialist author otherwise sensible

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in hurry or you'll be late
well can mean advisable or sensible, as in it would be well to wait

explanation.surface: A left-wing writer who is, by contrast, level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Animal Farm described himself as a democratic socialist.

clue.text: In grass, sex with Victor's given new vitality

indicators.note: the opening word puts the later pieces in the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
sex is Latin for six, the Roman numeral VI
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A romp in the long grass with Victor has put a spring in someone's step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought back to life or strength is restored and reinvigorated.

clue.text: Out to an extent in chair round Land's End

indicators.note: the seated word goes round the last letter of Land

parts.note: someone in a chair is seated

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Sitting in a chair at Land's End, partly nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of Cornwall. The definition is 'Out to an extent': someone drugged is semi-conscious.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugged patient is calmed and drowsy, partly unconscious.

clue.text: Island nation's heavyweight state?

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Pacific islands country is a weighty power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polynesian kingdom is a sovereign country made up of Pacific islands.

clue.text: Rose for example worker planted in row

indicators.note: something planted in a row is set inside it

parts.note: a line is a row
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A gardener's note: a rose, say, set by a worker in a row of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb (got up); it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbriar, a wild flower of the genus Rosa, is a species of the flower.

clue.text: Small island about to disappear

indicators.note: the about word is made to disappear from the island

parts.note: Minorca is a Balearic island
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A small island looks set to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor is of little size or importance.

clue.text: Seeing vegetable, suddenly collapse?

parts.note: to keel over is to collapse suddenly; the vegetable written over, backwards, spells keel

explanation.surface: Someone faints at the sight of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse idea: 'keel over' means collapse suddenly, and the vegetable written over, backwards, is KEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion-family plant with a long white stem is a vegetable.

clue.text: Items for kitchen meal, saving time, are set by wife

indicators.note: the meal saves or keeps the time inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: are is set by, next to, the wife, which comes first

explanation.surface: Kitchen things: a meal served promptly, with the wife setting out the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, pans and utensils of metal are household goods used in cooking.
